title: Capital Gains Tax Maths Differs Across Gold, Silver, Debt, & Equity ETFs
description: The capital gains tax on ETFs varies significantly based on the underlying asset class and holding period. Equity ETFs enjoy preferential tax treatment for lo.

faq.q: What is the difference between an ETF and a mutual fund for tax purposes?
faq.a: For tax purposes, ETFs are generally treated similarly to mutual funds, with distinctions primarily based on the underlying asset class (equity, debt, gold, etc.) rather than the fund structure itself.

faq.q: Do I get indexation benefit for Gold ETFs?
faq.a: For Gold ETFs purchased on or after April 1, 2023, the indexation benefit for long-term capital gains has been removed. All gains are now taxed at your income slab rate. For units purchased before this date, indexation benefit for LTCG (held over 36 months) still applies.

faq.q: Is LTCG on equity ETFs completely tax-free?
faq.a: No, LTCG on equity ETFs is exempt up to ₹1 lakh in a financial year. Gains exceeding this limit are taxed at 10% (plus surcharge and cess), without indexation benefit.

faq.q: How does the new tax regime affect my existing Debt ETF investments?
faq.a: The new tax regime (where gains are taxed at slab rates) only applies to Debt ETF units purchased on or after April 1, 2023. Your existing investments made before this date will continue to be governed by the old rules, including indexation benefit for LTCG.

faq.q: What is the holding period for LTCG in equity ETFs?
faq.a: For equity ETFs, the holding period to qualify for Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG) is more than 12 months.

faq.q: Are there any specific exemptions for NRI investors on ETF capital gains?
faq.a: Taxation for NRIs on capital gains from ETFs generally follows the same rules as resident Indians, but Double Taxation Avoidance Agreements (DTAA) with their country of residence might offer some relief. It's advisable for NRIs to consult a tax expert.
